items.name: Public Servers
items.access: Join the experience normally or choose Public Servers from the gamemodes menu.
items.objective: Fight in the standard Shinjuku-inspired public map with normal combat, item spawns, and public-server chaos.
items.playersTeams: Public server; Roblox API lists max players as 20.
items.lives: Normal respawns; no match life pool is listed.
items.winCondition: No round win condition. Keep fighting, practicing, and building normal kill or quest progress.
items.rewardSummary: Public and Ranked kills grant $5 when the kill credit rules count the damage.
items.progressionImpact: Best general route for normal practice, public fights, kill credit, daily or weekly quest progress, and cash from counted kills.
items.specialRules: Items spawn around the main map every 10 minutes, and most of the public map is destructible.
items.verificationNote: Gamemodes page confirms Public Servers and item spawn timing; Roblox API confirms 20 max players; Shop page confirms $5 public/ranked kill cash.

items.name: Casual Duels
items.access: Choose Duels, select Casual, then press Ready to search for an opponent or party matchup.
items.objective: Win a small-team duel by draining the opposing team's lives or ending the timer with more lives remaining.
items.playersTeams: 1v1, 2v2, and larger party duels; parties can hold up to 4 players and match same-size parties.
items.lives: 3 team lives in 1v1; 5 team lives in 2v2 and larger duels.
items.mapPool: Randomized duel maps such as Grass Field, Gym, Sewers, and Tombs of the Star.
items.winCondition: Deplete the other team's lives, or have more lives remaining when the timer ends.
items.rewardSummary: Normal kill cash can apply to counted kills; Casual does not use Elo.
items.progressionImpact: Best clean practice route before Ranked because it has duel structure without Elo loss.
items.specialRules: Casual adds Binding Vows at match start and allows up to two rematch votes after a duel.
items.verificationNote: Duels source confirms Casual, party size, lives, win condition, Binding Vows, and rematches.
items.imageStatus: local row-specific wiki screenshot or mode icon

items.name: Ranked Duels
items.access: Choose Duels, select Ranked, then press Ready to search for an Elo-based matchup.
items.objective: Win the duel under Ranked matchmaking rules and protect or gain Elo.
items.playersTeams: 1v1, 2v2, and larger same-size party duels through matchmaking.
items.lives: 3 team lives in 1v1; 5 team lives in 2v2 and larger duels.
items.mapPool: Randomized duel maps; Ranked destruction has been disabled by update-log rules.
items.winCondition: Deplete the other team's lives, or have more lives remaining when the timer ends.
items.rewardSummary: Ranked wins and losses change Elo; counted kills can still grant $5, but winning Ranked itself does not add a separate cash reward.
items.progressionImpact: Best route for competitive pressure and Elo, not for relaxed practice.
items.specialRules: No Binding Vows. Players start from 0 Elo, cannot drop below 0, and matchmaking avoids opponents with a 50+ Elo gap.
items.verificationNote: Duels source confirms Ranked Elo, no Binding Vows, life rules, and Elo gain/loss range. Shop trivia confirms no separate Ranked win cash.

items.name: Brain Swap (SWP)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Score as many kills as possible with randomized base and awakening movesets.
items.playersTeams: Roulette lobby players; individual kill race.
items.lives: No fixed life limit is listed; each death reshuffles the moveset.
items.winCondition: Finish with the strongest kill/point performance when the round ends.
items.rewardSummary: Kills grant Roulette points; round rewards are point-based and cap at $50.
items.progressionImpact: Good for fast random-kit practice and Roulette cash, but kills do not count as normal kill rewards.
items.specialRules: Moves come from the game's move pool with reduced damage/cooldowns, while some abilities and domain expansions are excluded.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table lists SWP as a Roulette minigame and reward table lists SWP kill points.
items.imageStatus: local row-specific wiki screenshot or mode icon

items.name: Sorcery Clash (SRC)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Win a team deathmatch as Sorcerers or Curses.
items.winCondition: The round ends when one team loses all players or the timer expires.
items.rewardSummary: Kills grant Roulette points; round rewards are point-based and cap at $50.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette pick for simple team fights and quick kill-point scoring.
items.specialRules: Friendly team structure is different from some Ranked team rules, where teammates may still harm each other in certain formats.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table lists SRC as team deathmatch; update log confirms SRC gives points for kills.
items.imageStatus: local row-specific wiki screenshot or mode icon

items.name: First to Twelve (FTT)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Reach 12 kills first while rotating through shared randomized base movesets.
items.playersTeams: Roulette lobby players; individual kill race.
items.winCondition: First player to reach 12 kills wins.
items.rewardSummary: Kills grant Roulette points; round rewards are point-based and cap at $50.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette mode for pure base-move fighting and quick kill-race practice.
items.specialRules: No Awakenings, regeneration, or burst. Each kill count changes the moveset, and 11 kills leaves Head Splitter as the only move.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table and V1.76 update log confirm FTT uses large maps and no passive regeneration, bursts, or Awakening moves.
items.imageStatus: local row-specific wiki screenshot or mode icon

items.name: Final Showdown (FSD)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Defeat the Strongest Of History boss as Sorcerers, or drain all Sorcerer lives as the boss.
items.playersTeams: One random boss against the Sorcerers team.
items.lives: Sorcerers get 3 lives each. The boss has 1 life.
items.winCondition: Sorcerers win by killing the boss. The boss wins by draining Sorcerer lives or surviving the 6-minute timer.
items.rewardSummary: Damage dealt decides points for both Sorcerers and the boss; rewards cap at $50. The boss can earn a special Victory Flash.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette pick for team focus and damage-based scoring instead of pure kill racing.
items.specialRules: The boss's health scales with active players, and neither side regenerates health.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table and reward table list FSD role, lives, timer, no regeneration, and damage-based scoring.
items.imageStatus: local row-specific wiki screenshot or mode icon

items.name: End of Journey (EOJ)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Survive as Sorcerers until the timer ends, or turn every Sorcerer into a Transfigured Human as Curses.
items.playersTeams: Sorcerers versus Curses created by defeated Sorcerers.
items.lives: Sorcerers have one life. Defeated Sorcerers respawn as Transfigured Humans with infinite lives.
items.winCondition: Sorcerers win by surviving the timer. Curses win by converting every Sorcerer before time runs out.
items.rewardSummary: Sorcerer kills grant points. Curse rewards use both kills and damage dealt. Round rewards cap at $50.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette mode for survival pressure and team conversion rules.
items.specialRules: Transfigured Humans have 20 HP, no front dash, varying movesets after death, and Locust Guy M1s. Parkour is disabled.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table lists EOJ as wave/infection survival; trivia notes older SRC/EOJ naming changes but current row is retained.
items.imageStatus: local row-specific wiki screenshot or mode icon

items.name: Perfection Tag (PFT)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Run from the Perfection player as Sorcerers, or tag players as Perfection.
items.playersTeams: One Perfection tagger against defenseless Sorcerers.
items.lives: Sorcerers have 1 HP and combat disabled; the source does not list a normal respawn pool.
items.winCondition: Sorcerers survive until the timer ends; the tagger tries to catch them before time runs out.
items.rewardSummary: Runners gain points from time spent near the tagger. The tagger gains points from kills. Round rewards cap at $50.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette mode for movement, panic routing, and nonstandard scoring.
items.specialRules: Each death extends the timer by 15 seconds, capped at 3 minutes. The tagger has a faster no-cooldown Idle Transfiguration move.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table and reward table list PFT role split, timer extension, 1 HP runners, and scoring rules.

items.name: American Shenanigans (AMS)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Shoot crows with an infinite-ammo gun and build progress points.
items.playersTeams: All players are placed on the same team with friendly fire.
items.winCondition: Reach strong point progress and perform well before the round ends.
items.rewardSummary: Kills and accuracy decide points. Round rewards cap at $50.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette mode for aim-focused scoring instead of normal moveset fighting.
items.specialRules: Players receive an undroppable gun. At 40 progress points, a player gets the faster God Gun that can bypass friendly fire.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table lists AMS rules; V1.74 update log says AMS was reworked with more content.
items.imageStatus: local row-specific wiki screenshot or mode icon

items.name: Prison Realm (PSR)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Avoid being sealed by passing the Prison Realm to another player before the timer expires.
items.playersTeams: All players in a free-for-all domain-clash state.
items.lives: The source describes sealed players being killed; no separate respawn pool is listed.
items.rewardSummary: Specific PSR point scoring is not listed; treat the mode as Roulette variety rather than a planned scoring route.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette mode for movement, tag pressure, and last-player-standing reactions, not for predictable point planning.
items.specialRules: Movesets are overridden by domain clash state. The tagged player gets a 15-second Prison Realm timer, faster walk speed, double side dashes, and weaker melee.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table lists PSR as active, and search only found the Gamemodes page for PSR points. The reward table has no PSR-specific scoring row, so scoring is intentionally left unpromised.

items.name: Soul Swap (SSP)
items.access: Choose Roulette, select a region, then vote in the Roulette lobby.
items.objective: Choose from random moveset offers after spawning and score as many kills as possible.
items.playersTeams: Roulette lobby players; individual kill race.
items.lives: No fixed life limit is listed; each death reshuffles the moveset choices.
items.winCondition: Finish with the strongest kill/point performance when the round ends.
items.rewardSummary: Kills grant Roulette points; round rewards are point-based and cap at $50.
items.progressionImpact: Best Roulette mode for testing random character mechanics and custom Skill Builder movesets.
items.specialRules: Players choose from 3 random movesets with Common, Rare, and Legendary rarities. Some offers are custom-made through Skill Builder.
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes table lists SSP as active and reward table groups SSP with kill-point Roulette modes.

items.name: Custom Servers
items.access: Choose Custom Server, refresh/search the list or enter a region, then join a hosted server; hosting uses Create A Server and a server title.
items.objective: Use player-hosted private servers for builds, movesets, tournaments, private commands, and controlled practice.
items.playersTeams: Player-hosted server; team rules depend on private-server settings.
items.lives: Depends on private-server settings and the activity being hosted.
items.mapPool: Private server map with owner-controlled commands, Workshop presets, and build/custom options.
items.winCondition: No single win condition. The host's rules, commands, build, or tournament format decide the goal.
items.rewardSummary: Private-server rows are mainly for practice and custom play. Items and sodas are free in private servers.
items.progressionImpact: Best for labbing moves, using dummies, testing builds, hosting tournaments, and practicing without normal public-server pressure.
items.specialRules: Owners can adjust server settings such as destruction, friendly fire, damage, walk speed, dummies, Workshop access, free build, cooldowns, and player controls.
items.verificationNote: Gamemodes page confirms custom server join/host flow; Private Servers page confirms owner commands and free items/sodas.

items.name: Creator Clash
items.access: Choose Creator Clash from the gamemodes menu; no current extra access requirement is listed.
items.objective: Fight on a special map using custom characters and movesets uploaded through the Workshop.
items.playersTeams: Public Creator Clash match; exact team rules are not listed.
items.lives: No fixed life pool is listed.
items.winCondition: Fight with custom movesets. A single exact match win condition is not listed.
items.rewardSummary: No specific cash or point reward is listed for Creator Clash.
items.progressionImpact: Best for custom-moveset fighting after normal combat basics and Workshop access make sense.
items.specialRules: Creator Clash uses Workshop custom characters and applies limits to visual effects, abilities, damage per second, sound volume, and broken custom movesets.
items.sourceStatus: Current source-backed; older update-log requirement superseded by current Gamemodes wording
items.verificationNote: Current Gamemodes page says Creator Clash grants access to all players. Older V1.73/V1.74 update-log notes mention a kill requirement that was later reduced to 30, but the checked current mode page does not keep that requirement.
